{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01SqmLwJhEBvrfYJLkZpYpEz","type":"tool_result","content":"1\tusing Guardrails.Core.Graph;\n2\t\n3\tnamespace Guardrails.Core.Tests;\n4\t\n5\t/// <summary>\n6\t/// Unit tests for <see cref=\"HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render\"/> (issue #33): the self-contained local\n7\t/// <c>diagram.html</c> viewer. Pure string mapping — no disk. Pins the provenance line, the\n8\t/// verbatim-source embedding, the interaction prerequisites (loose security for clicks, pan/zoom,\n9\t/// fullscreen), determinism, and newline normalization.\n10\t/// </summary>\n11\tpublic sealed class HtmlDiagramRendererTests\n12\t{\n13\t    private const string Hash = \"abc123def456\";\n14\t    private const string Source = \"flowchart TD\\n  task_a[\\\"a\\\"]:::task\\n  classDef task fill:#cfe8ff;\";\n15\t\n16\t    private static readonly IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> NoTargets =\n17\t        new Dictionary<string, string>(StringComparer.Ordinal);\n18\t\n19\t    private static readonly IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> OneTarget =\n20\t        new Dictionary<string, string>(StringComparer.Ordinal) { [\"task_01_a\"] = \"tasks/01-a/\" };\n21\t\n22\t    [Fact]\n23\t    public void Render_FirstLine_IsProvenanceComment_WithSameHash()\n24\t    {\n25\t        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, NoTargets);\n26\t        string firstLine = html.Split('\\n')[0];\n27\t\n28\t        // Same provenance shape as diagram.md, and FIRST so the \\A-anchored reader (graph --check)\n29\t        // matches it in both files.\n30\t        Assert.Equal($\"<!-- guardrails:graph v1 source-sha256={Hash} -->\", firstLine);\n31\t    }\n32\t\n33\t    [Fact]\n34\t    public void Render_EmbedsSourceVerbatim_InRawTextScript()\n35\t    {\n36\t        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, NoTargets);\n37\t\n38\t        Assert.Contains(\"type=\\\"text/plain\\\"\", html);\n39\t        Assert.Contains(Source, html); // verbatim — not interpolated into a JS string\n40\t        Assert.Contains(\"<!doctype html>\", html);\n41\t    }\n42\t\n43\t    [Fact]\n44\t    public void Render_EnablesClicksAndNavigation()\n45\t    {\n46\t        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, NoTargets);\n47\t\n48\t        // Clicks (node -> source file) only fire when mermaid runs in 'loose' security.\n49\t        Assert.Contains(\"securityLevel: 'loose'\", html);\n50\t        // Pan/zoom + fullscreen affordances.\n51\t        Assert.Contains(\"svg-pan-zoom\", html);\n52\t        Assert.Contains(\"requestFullscreen\", html);\n53\t    }\n54\t\n55\t    [Fact]\n56\t    public void Render_RaisesMermaidSizeCeilings_SoLargeDagsRender()\n57\t    {\n58\t        // Issue #108: a large plan's DAG source exceeds Mermaid's default 50 000-char maxTextSize\n59\t        // and/or 500-edge maxEdges ceiling, so mermaid.render throws and the page falls back to\n60\t        // \"could not render\". The fix lifts BOTH ceilings in mermaid.initialize — assert they are\n61\t        // present (a regression that drops either re-introduces the big-plan render failure).\n62\t        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, NoTargets);\n63\t\n64\t        Assert.Contains(\"maxTextSize: 5000000\", html);\n65\t        Assert.Contains(\"maxEdges: 100000\", html);\n66\t    }\n67\t\n68\t    [Fact]\n69\t    public void Render_IsDeterministic()\n70\t    {\n71\t        Assert.Equal(\n72\t            HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget),\n73\t            HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget));\n74\t    }\n75\t\n76\t    [Fact]\n77\t    public void Render_NormalizesCrlf_NoCarriageReturnsInOutput()\n78\t    {\n79\t        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(\"flowchart TD\\r\\n  a-->b\\r\\n\", Hash, NoTargets);\n80\t        Assert.DoesNotContain('\\r', html);\n81\t    }\n82\t\n83\t    [Fact]\n84\t    public void Render_EmptyHash_Throws()\n85\t    {\n86\t        Assert.Throws<ArgumentException>(() => HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, \"\", NoTargets));\n87\t    }\n88\t\n89\t    [Fact]\n90\t    public void Render_NullTaskFolderTargets_Throws()\n91\t    {\n92\t        Assert.Throws<ArgumentNullException>(() => HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, null!));\n93\t    }\n94\t\n95\t    // === legend overlay (outside the Mermaid graph; see MermaidRenderer remarks) =======\n96\t\n97\t    [Fact]\n98\t    public void Render_IncludesALegendOverlayDiv_OutsideTheEmbeddedMermaidSource()\n99\t    {\n100\t        // A Mermaid-native legend was prototyped and rendered broken headless (dagre treats a\n101\t        // disconnected subgraph as a phantom extra \"task\"); the only working placement is an HTML\n102\t        // overlay div outside the embedded Mermaid <script> source, mirroring #bar/#hint.\n103\t        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, NoTargets);\n104\t\n105\t This test would have caught\n209\t        // the regression: `Assert.Contains(\"'transparent'\")` alone passes for EITHER form.\n210\t        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, Assert.Contains(\"{}\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n238\t    }\n239\t\n240\t    // === long task-name title wrap-overflow fix (issue cluster-label-wrap-overflow) ====\n241\t    //\n242\t    // Mermaid always wraps a cluster's title <div> to a hardcoded 200px width (bundled\n243\t    // mermaid@11.4.1's plain flowchart cluster shape never overrides createText's width=200\n244\t    // default), and dagre's layout pass reserves the container's header-strip height BEFORE that\n245\t    // wrapped height is known — so a long kebab-case task name that wraps to 2+ lines prints past\n246\t    // the reserved strip, overlapping the first leaf guardrail/preflight box below it. No Mermaid\n247\t    // config knob avoids this (verified against the bundled 11.4.1 source). The fix re-wraps the\n248\t    // SAME text at up to the container's own (already wider) width post-render instead, verified\n249\t    // headless against 8+ real plans (40+ long task names, container widths ~230px-~1100px,\n250\t    // wraps of 2-3 lines): every case converged to one line with the same healthy gap a\n251\t    // never-wrapped label already has, and every already-fits label was left byte-for-byte\n252\t    // unchanged (including the whole golden hello-guardrails example).\n253\t\n254\t    [Fact]\n255\t    public void Render_DefinesFixWrappedClusterLabelsFunction()\n256\t    {\n257\t        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget);\n258\t\n259\t        Assert.Contains(\"function fixWrappedClusterLabels(svgEl)\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n260\t    }\n261\t\n262\t    [Fact]\n263\t    public void Render_WrapFix_RunsAfterMermaidRenderResolves_AndBeforeTheOverlay()\n264\t    {\n265\t        // Ordering is load-bearing: addTaskContainerOverlays measures the label's CURRENT bbox to\n266\t        // size its click band, so a label the wrap fix already shrank back to one line must be\n267\t        // fixed FIRST, or the band would be sized for the original (possibly multi-line) wrap.\n268\t        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget);\n269\t\n270\t        int renderCall = html.IndexOf(\"await mermaid.render(\", StringComparison.Ordinal);\n271\t        int wrapFixInvocation = html.IndexOf(\"fixWrappedClusterLabels(\", renderCall, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n272\t        int overlayInvocation = html.IndexOf(\"addTaskContainerOverlays(\", renderCall, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n273\t\n274\t        Assert.True(renderCall >= 0 && wrapFixInvocation > renderCall && overlayInvocation > renderCall,\n275\t            \"both post-render fixes must be invoked after the render call\");\n276\t        Assert.True(wrapFixInvocation < overlayInvocation,\n277\t            \"the wrap fix must run BEFORE the title-band overlay so the band reflects the corrected label size\");\n278\t    }\n279\t\n280\t    [Fact]\n281\t    public void Render_WrapFix_MeasuresViaScrollWidth_NotGetBoundingClientRect()\n282\t    {\n283\t        // Regression guard for the exact measurement pitfall this fix's own investigation hit:\n284\t        // height attributes. scrollWidth/scrollHeight are local layout-box measurements, in the\n287\t        // SAME coordinate system as those attributes, regardless of the current zoom level.\n288\t        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget);\n289\t\n290\t        int fnStart = html.IndexOf(\"function fixWrappedClusterLabels\", StringComparison.Ordinal);\n291\t        int fnEnd = html.IndexOf(\"\\n}\\n\", fnStart, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n292\t        string fnBody = html[fnStart..fnEnd];\n293\t\n294\t        Assert.Contains(\"div.scrollWidth\", fnBody, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n295\t        Assert.Contains(\"div.scrollHeight\", fnBody, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n296\t        Assert.DoesNotContain(\"getBoundingClientRect\", fnBody, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n297\t    }\n298\t\n299\t    [Fact]\n300\t    public void Render_WrapFix_NeverNarrowsBelowMermaidsOriginalWidth()\n301\t    {\n302\t        // The fix only ever WIDENS a StringComparison.Ordinal);\n308\t    }\n309\t\n310\t    [Fact]\n311\t    public void Render_WrapFix_SkipsLabelsThatAlreadyFitOnOneLine()\n312\t    {\n313\t        // Short names (e.g. every task in StringComparison.Ordinal);\n340\t    }\n341\t\n342\t    // === live per-node status overlay (issue #219) =====================================\n343\t    //\n344\t    // While a `guardrails run` is in progress, diagram.html gains a small corner-anchored status\n345\t    // badge on each task container, preflight/guardrail leaf, and the plan-level Full Flight Checks\n346\t    // / Terminal Gate brackets: an animated spinner while running, a settled check/X/\"?\" glyph once\n347\t    // finished — driven by an OPTIONAL per-node status map plus an INDEPENDENT includeRefresh\n348\t    // toggle, mirroring LogSiteRenderer.IndexHtml(..., includeRefresh)'s during-run/final duality.\n349\t    //\n350\t    // These tests are structural/string-content assertions over the emitted HTML/JS (no headless\n351\t    // browser is configured in this repo — a documented Level-A gap): they prove the right markup\n352\t    // and data are EMITTED, not that a browser positions the badges pixel-correctly at runtime. The\n353\t    // four non-null-status tests are the intended TDD RED against the throwing stub — the\n354\t    // 02-implement-diagram-status-overlay-renderer task turns them green.\n355\t    //\n356\t    // Status-map ids use the SAME vocabulary MermaidRenderer emits (task containers `task_<base>`,\n357\t    // preflight/guardrail leaves `task_<base>_pf_<n>`/`task_<base>_gr_<n>`, and the two plan-level\n358\t    // brackets `plan_preflights`/`plan_guardrails`) so the post-render overlay script can position a\n359\t    // badge on the matching SVG node. All five status values are exercised.\n360\t    private static readonly IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> SampleStatuses =\n361\t        new Dictionary<string, string>(StringComparer.Ordinal)\n362\t        {\n363\t            [\"plan_preflights\"] = \"passed\",       // Full Flight Checks bracket (top)\n364\t            [\"task_root\"] = \"running\",            // a task container, mid-run -> spinner\n365\t            [\"task_root_pf_0\"] = \"passed\",        // a preflight leaf check\n366\t            [\"task_root_gr_0\"] = \"failed\",        // a guardrail leaf check\n367\t            [\"task_next\"] = \"pending\",            // a not-yet-started task container\n368\t            [\"plan_guardrails\"] = \"needs-human\",  // Terminal Gate bracket (bottom)\n369\t        };\n370\t\n371\t    [Fact]\n372\t    public void Render_WithNullNodeStatuses_IsByteIdenticalToCurrentBehavior()\n373\t    {\n374\t        // The static `graph` command path (no live status) must be UNCHANGED by this feature: the\n375\t        // pre-existing three-argument overload and the new call passing nodeStatuses:null must\n376\t        // produce the exact same document, byte-for-byte — the golden fixtures\n377\t        // (examples/hello-guardrails, docs/plans/08-parallel-execution/diagram.html) are out of this\n378\t        // task's scope and must not need regenerating.\n379\t        string legacy = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget);\n380\t        string newNull = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget, nodeStatuses: null);\n381\t\n382\t        Assert.Equal(legacy, newNull);\n383\t\n384\t        // ...and the static path carries NONE of the live-overlay markers. Each of these is absent\n385\t        // from today's template, so their absence pins the null path clean — a leak of the feature\n386\t        // into the static path (which would silently change every checked-in diagram.html) fails here.\n387\t        Assert.DoesNotContain(\"http-equiv=\\\"refresh\\\"\", newNull, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n388\t        Assert.DoesNotContain(\"@keyframes\", newNull, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n389\t        Assert.DoesNotContain(\"id=\\\"node-statuses\\\"\", newNull, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n390\t    }\n391\t\n392\t    [Fact]\n393\t    public void Render_WithNodeStatuses_EmitsAMetaRefreshTag()\n394\t    {\n395\t        // A non-null status map with the default includeRefresh:true is the DURING-RUN diagram — it\n396\t        // must carry <meta http-equiv=\"refresh\"> so a plain file:// view re-reads itself as the run\n397\t        // progresses (mirrors LogSiteRenderer's during-run index). The static (null) path must not.\n398\t        string live = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget, SampleStatuses);\n399\t        Assert.Contains(\"<meta http-equiv=\\\"refresh\\\"\", live, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n400\t\n401\t        string stat = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget, nodeStatuses: null);\n402\t        Assert.DoesNotContain(\"http-equiv=\\\"refresh\\\"\", stat, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n403\t    }\n404\t\n405\t    [Fact]\n406\t    public void Render_WithNodeStatusesAndIncludeRefreshFalse_OmitsTheMetaRefreshTag()\n407\t    {\n408\t        // The FINAL settled render (wired at run-end by 06-wire-diagramobserver-into-runcommand):\n409\t        // nodeStatuses is STILL non-null (every node shows its final settled status) but\n410\t        // includeRefresh:false, so the auto-reload tag is dropped — the page is done refreshing. The\n411\t        // status overlay itself must STILL be emitted (the refresh tag and the overlay are independent).\n412\t        string settled = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(\n413\t            Source, Hash, OneTarget, SampleStatuses, includeRefresh: false);\n414\t\n415\t        Assert.DoesNotContain(\"http-equiv=\\\"refresh\\\"\", settled, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n416\t        // still a live-status document — the overlay data is present regardless of includeRefresh.\n417\t        Assert.Contains(\"id=\\\"node-statuses\\\"\", settled, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n418\t        Assert.Contains(\"\\\"task_root\\\"\", settled, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n419\t    }\n420\t\n421\t    [Fact]\n422\t    public void Render_WithNodeStatuses_EmitsAnOverlayForEachStatusEntry()\n423\t    {\n424\t        // Every node id in the status map must be referenced by the overlay-rendering logic — the\n425\t        // map is embedded as a JSON side-table (mirroring the task-folder-targets side-table) keyed\n426\t        // by the SAME Mermaid node/container ids, so the post-render script can position a badge on\n427\t        // each matching SVG node. Assert the QUOTED (JSON-key) form: a bare-word check would false-\n428\t        // positive on ids like `plan_guardrails` that ALREADY appear in a code comment in today's\n429\t        // template — only the emitted status map produces the quoted form.\n430\t        string live = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget, SampleStatuses);\n431\t\n432\t        foreach (string nodeId in SampleStatuses.Keys)\n433\t        {\n434\t            Assert.Contains($\"\\\"{nodeId}\\\"\", live, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n435\t        }\n436\t    }\n437\t\n438\t    [Fact]\n439\t    public void Render_WithRunningStatus_EmitsASpinnerClass_AndSettledStatusesEmitAGlyph()\n440\t    {\n441\t        // \"running\" must render an ANIMATED spinner (a CSS @keyframes rotation — no external\n442\t        // image/GIF dependency), visibly distinct from a settled status's STATIC glyph (check / X /\n443\t        // \"?\"). Assert both the spinner animation + its dedicated class AND at least one settled\n444\t        // glyph are present; the spinner marker (a CSS class) is inherently distinct from the glyph\n445\t        // characters, so a spinner can never be mistaken for a settled state.\n446\t        string live = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget, SampleStatuses);\n447\t\n448\t        // spinner: a CSS keyframes rotation + a dedicated class (neither exists in the static template).\n449\t        Assert.Contains(\"@keyframes\", live, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n450\t        Assert.Contains(\"status-spinner\", live, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n451\t\n452\t        // settled glyphs: `passed` -> U+2713 CHECK MARK, `failed` -> U+2717 BALLOT X (both present in\n453\t        // SampleStatuses). Written as literal UTF-8 glyphs; this file is valid UTF-8, which Roslyn's\n454\t        // BOM-less source detection decodes as UTF-8, so the literals compile to exactly these chars.\n455\t        Assert.Contains(\"✓\", live, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n456\t        Assert.Contains(\"✗\", live, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n457\t    }\n458\t}\n459\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"947025b1-00ab-45d6-bec4-5dec3305bac9","uuid":"e40d993a-7a4c-4492-ad62-f8ddfdcd50e7","timestamp":"2026-07-07T16:17:53.771Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"C:\\Users\\David\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\guardrails-worktrees\\diagram-live-status-and-search-80c8913d\\1bb6c1ff\\07-author-tests-diagram-search-box\\attempt-1\\tests\\Guardrails.Core.Tests\\HtmlDiagramRendererTests.cs","content":"using Guardrails.Core.Graph;\n\nnamespace Guardrails.Core.Tests;\n\n/// <summary>\n/// Unit tests for <see cref=\"HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render\"/> (issue #33): the self-contained local\n/// <c>diagram.html</c> viewer. Pure string mapping — no disk. Pins the provenance line, the\n/// verbatim-source embedding, the interaction prerequisites (loose security for clicks, pan/zoom,\n/// fullscreen), determinism, and newline normalization.\n/// </summary>\npublic sealed class HtmlDiagramRendererTests\n{\n    private const string Hash = \"abc123def456\";\n    private const string Source = \"flowchart TD\\n  task_a[\\\"a\\\"]:::task\\n  classDef task fill:#cfe8ff;\";\n\n    private static readonly IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> NoTargets =\n        new Dictionary<string, string>(StringComparer.Ordinal);\n\n    private static readonly IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> OneTarget =\n        new Dictionary<string, string>(StringComparer.Ordinal) { [\"task_01_a\"] = \"tasks/01-a/\" };\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_FirstLine_IsProvenanceComment_WithSameHash()\n    {\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, NoTargets);\n        string firstLine = html.Split('\\n')[0];\n\n        // Same provenance shape as diagram.md, and FIRST so the \\A-anchored reader (graph --check)\n        // matches it in both files.\n        Assert.Equal($\"<!-- guardrails:graph v1 source-sha256={Hash} -->\", firstLine);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_EmbedsSourceVerbatim_InRawTextScript()\n    {\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, NoTargets);\n\n        Assert.Contains(\"type=\\\"text/plain\\\"\", html);\n        Assert.Contains(Source, html); // verbatim — not interpolated into a JS string\n        Assert.Contains(\"<!doctype html>\", html);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_EnablesClicksAndNavigation()\n    {\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, NoTargets);\n\n        // Clicks (node -> source file) only fire when mermaid runs in 'loose' security.\n        Assert.Contains(\"securityLevel: 'loose'\", html);\n        // Pan/zoom + fullscreen affordances.\n        Assert.Contains(\"svg-pan-zoom\", html);\n        Assert.Contains(\"requestFullscreen\", html);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_RaisesMermaidSizeCeilings_SoLargeDagsRender()\n    {\n        // Issue #108: a large plan's DAG source exceeds Mermaid's default 50 000-char maxTextSize\n        // and/or 500-edge maxEdges ceiling, so mermaid.render throws and the page falls back to\n        // \"could not render\". The fix lifts BOTH ceilings in mermaid.initialize — assert they are\n        // present (a regression that drops either re-introduces the big-plan render failure).\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, NoTargets);\n\n        Assert.Contains(\"maxTextSize: 5000000\", html);\n        Assert.Contains(\"maxEdges: 100000\", html);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_IsDeterministic()\n    {\n        Assert.Equal(\n            HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget),\n            HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget));\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_NormalizesCrlf_NoCarriageReturnsInOutput()\n    {\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(\"flowchart TD\\r\\n  a-->b\\r\\n\", Hash, NoTargets);\n        Assert.DoesNotContain('\\r', html);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_EmptyHash_Throws()\n    {\n        Assert.Throws<ArgumentException>(() => HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, \"\", NoTargets));\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_NullTaskFolderTargets_Throws()\n    {\n        Assert.Throws<ArgumentNullException>(() => HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, null!));\n    }\n\n    // === legend overlay (outside the Mermaid graph; see MermaidRenderer remarks) =======\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_IncludesALegendOverlayDiv_OutsideTheEmbeddedMermaidSource()\n    {\n        // A Mermaid-native legend was prototyped and rendered broken headless (dagre treats a\n        // disconnected subgraph as a phantom extra \"task\"); the only working placement is an HTML\n        // overlay div outside the embedded Mermaid <script> source, mirroring #bar/#hint.\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, NoTargets);\n\n        Assert.Contains(\"id=\\\"legend\\\"\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_LegendOverlay_StatesBothAColorAndABeforeAfterTimingWord()\n    {\n        // A bare category name would not preserve the \"preflights run before, guardrails run\n        // after\" semantic the removed nested boxes used to convey visually — the legend must spell\n        // out both the colour mapping AND the timing/consequence in words.\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, NoTargets);\n\n        Assert.Contains(\"Preflight\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.Contains(\"Guardrail\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.Contains(\"BEFORE\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.Contains(\"AFTER\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_LegendOverlay_IsNotInsideTheEmbeddedGraphSourceScript()\n    {\n        // The legend must live OUTSIDE the raw-text <script id=\"graph-source\"> element — it is\n        // not part of the Mermaid source, so it can never affect anything that parses that source\n        // (rendering) or hashes it (GraphSourceHash, via MermaidRenderer.SemanticContent).\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, NoTargets);\n\n        int scriptStart = html.IndexOf(\"id=\\\"graph-source\\\"\", StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        int scriptEnd = html.IndexOf(\"</script>\", scriptStart, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        string scriptContent = html[scriptStart..scriptEnd];\n\n        Assert.DoesNotContain(\"legend\", scriptContent, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n\n    // === task-container title-band overlay (issue #232/#233 superseded, issue #235) ====\n    //\n    // The Mermaid-source anchor-node mechanism (#211) proved useless in practice — a real\n    // headless-Chrome measurement found the anchor covering only 0.44% of a content-dense\n    // container's area, off-center, missed by every realistic click point. The fix instead\n    // injects a post-render SVG overlay on the container's title/label band via JavaScript.\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_EmbedsTaskFolderTargets_AsJsonSideTable()\n    {\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget);\n\n        Assert.Contains(\"id=\\\"task-folder-targets\\\"\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.Contains(\"\\\"task_01_a\\\"\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.Contains(\"tasks/01-a/\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_NoLongerEmitsAnchorNodeMechanism()\n    {\n        // The #211 anchor-node click mechanism (Mermaid-source invisible node + classDef) is\n        // superseded entirely — HtmlDiagramRenderer must not reference it either.\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget);\n\n        Assert.DoesNotContain(\"classDef invisible\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_OverlayScript_AppendsToCluster_NotInsertsFirst()\n    {\n        // Load-bearing z-order fix: appendChild (not insertBefore as firstChild) — see class\n        // remarks and HtmlDiagramRenderer's remarks for why insertBefore silently blocks clicks\n        // (it lands the overlay BEHIND the cluster's own background rect).\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget);\n\n        Assert.Contains(\"cluster.appendChild(a)\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.DoesNotContain(\"insertBefore(a, cluster.firstChild\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_OverlayScript_ComputesBandFromClusterAndLabelBBox()\n    {\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget);\n\n        Assert.Contains(\"cluster.getBBox()\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.Contains(\"label.getBBox()\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.Contains(\".cluster-label\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_OverlayScript_UsesTransparentFill_NotNone()\n    {\n        // Same hit-testing hazard as the retired anchor node: fill:none is invisible to\n        // pointer-events:visiblePainted hit-testing; the overlay rect must use a painted-but-\n        // invisible transparent fill instead.\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget);\n\n        Assert.Contains(\"'transparent'\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_OverlayScript_SetsFillViaInlineStyle_NotTheFillAttribute()\n    {\n        // Real-browser regression (found live, not guessed): Mermaid's own generated stylesheet\n        // carries a rule shaped like `#dag .cluster rect{fill:<theme color>;...}`. Since the\n        // overlay rect is nested inside the .cluster group, that selector matches it too — and a\n        // CSS class/tag selector beats a plain HTML presentation attribute, so\n        // `rect.setAttribute('fill', 'transparent')` was silently overridden, painting a solid\n        // theme-colored bar over the container's title text (confirmed via getComputedStyle:\n        // attribute said \"transparent\", computed fill was the theme's cluster-background color).\n        // An inline style (`rect.style.fill = ...`) wins over any external/embedded stylesheet\n        // rule short of `!important`, so it reliably stays invisible. This test would have caught\n        // the regression: `Assert.Contains(\"'transparent'\")` alone passes for EITHER form.\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget);\n\n        Assert.Contains(\"rect.style.fill = 'transparent'\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.DoesNotContain(\"rect.setAttribute('fill'\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_OverlayScript_RunsAfterMermaidRenderResolves()\n    {\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget);\n\n        int renderCall = html.IndexOf(\"await mermaid.render(\", StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        int overlayDefinition = html.IndexOf(\"function addTaskContainerOverlays\", StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.True(renderCall >= 0 && overlayDefinition >= 0, \"both the render call and overlay function must be present\");\n\n        // The overlay must be INVOKED after the render call (the definition itself may appear\n        // earlier in the script — only invocation order matters for correctness).\n        int overlayInvocation = html.IndexOf(\"addTaskContainerOverlays(\", renderCall, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.True(overlayInvocation > renderCall, \"the overlay must be applied to the SVG mermaid.render just produced\");\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_EmptyTaskFolderTargets_StillRendersValidPage()\n    {\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, NoTargets);\n\n        Assert.Contains(\"id=\\\"task-folder-targets\\\"\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.Contains(\"{}\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n\n    // === long task-name title wrap-overflow fix (issue cluster-label-wrap-overflow) ====\n    //\n    // Mermaid always wraps a cluster's title <div> to a hardcoded 200px width (bundled\n    // mermaid@11.4.1's plain flowchart cluster shape never overrides createText's width=200\n    // default), and dagre's layout pass reserves the container's header-strip height BEFORE that\n    // wrapped height is known — so a long kebab-case task name that wraps to 2+ lines prints past\n    // the reserved strip, overlapping the first leaf guardrail/preflight box below it. No Mermaid\n    // config knob avoids this (verified against the bundled 11.4.1 source). The fix re-wraps the\n    // SAME text at up to the container's own (already wider) width post-render instead, verified\n    // headless against 8+ real plans (40+ long task names, container widths ~230px-~1100px,\n    // wraps of 2-3 lines): every case converged to one line with the same healthy gap a\n    // never-wrapped label already has, and every already-fits label was left byte-for-byte\n    // unchanged (including the whole golden hello-guardrails example).\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_DefinesFixWrappedClusterLabelsFunction()\n    {\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget);\n\n        Assert.Contains(\"function fixWrappedClusterLabels(svgEl)\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_WrapFix_RunsAfterMermaidRenderResolves_AndBeforeTheOverlay()\n    {\n        // Ordering is load-bearing: addTaskContainerOverlays measures the label's CURRENT bbox to\n        // size its click band, so a label the wrap fix already shrank back to one line must be\n        // fixed FIRST, or the band would be sized for the original (possibly multi-line) wrap.\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget);\n\n        int renderCall = html.IndexOf(\"await mermaid.render(\", StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        int wrapFixInvocation = html.IndexOf(\"fixWrappedClusterLabels(\", renderCall, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        int overlayInvocation = html.IndexOf(\"addTaskContainerOverlays(\", renderCall, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n\n        Assert.True(renderCall >= 0 && wrapFixInvocation > renderCall && overlayInvocation > renderCall,\n            \"both post-render fixes must be invoked after the render call\");\n        Assert.True(wrapFixInvocation < overlayInvocation,\n            \"the wrap fix must run BEFORE the title-band overlay so the band reflects the corrected label size\");\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_WrapFix_MeasuresViaScrollWidth_NotGetBoundingClientRect()\n    {\n        // Regression guard for the exact measurement pitfall this fix's own investigation hit:\n        // getBoundingClientRect() reports on-screen pixels affected by the page's pan-zoom\n        // transform, which is misleading when compared against a foreignObject's local width/\n        // height attributes. scrollWidth/scrollHeight are local layout-box measurements, in the\n        // SAME coordinate system as those attributes, regardless of the current zoom level.\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget);\n\n        int fnStart = html.IndexOf(\"function fixWrappedClusterLabels\", StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        int fnEnd = html.IndexOf(\"\\n}\\n\", fnStart, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        string fnBody = html[fnStart..fnEnd];\n\n        Assert.Contains(\"div.scrollWidth\", fnBody, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.Contains(\"div.scrollHeight\", fnBody, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.DoesNotContain(\"getBoundingClientRect\", fnBody, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_WrapFix_NeverNarrowsBelowMermaidsOriginalWidth()\n    {\n        // The fix only ever WIDENS a label (fewer lines needs less height, never more) — it must\n        // never choose a width narrower than what Mermaid already assigned, which would be a\n        // regression risking MORE wrapping, not less.\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget);\n\n        Assert.Contains(\"Math.max(currentWidth, clusterBox.width - 16)\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_WrapFix_SkipsLabelsThatAlreadyFitOnOneLine()\n    {\n        // Short names (e.g. every task in the golden hello-guardrails example) must be left\n        // completely untouched — this is the guard that makes that a no-op.\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget);\n\n        Assert.Contains(\"if (naturalWidth <= currentWidth) continue;\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_WrapFix_RevertsWhenWideningDoesNotReduceHeight()\n    {\n        // A container too narrow to help must fall back to Mermaid's original sizing rather than\n        // risk an oddly-proportioned label — never regress relative to the pre-fix rendering.\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget);\n\n        Assert.Contains(\"if (newHeight >= currentHeight)\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.Contains(\"div.setAttribute('style', savedInline);\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_WrapFix_RecentersTheLabelOnTheSameMidpointAfterWidening()\n    {\n        // Mermaid centers the label group via translate(x - bbox.width / 2, y); widening without\n        // re-centering would shift the (now wider) box off-center over the cluster.\n        string html = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget);\n\n        Assert.Contains(\"deltaCenter\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.Contains(\"label.setAttribute('transform',\", html, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n\n    // === live per-node status overlay (issue #219) =====================================\n    //\n    // While a `guardrails run` is in progress, diagram.html gains a small corner-anchored status\n    // badge on each task container, preflight/guardrail leaf, and the plan-level Full Flight Checks\n    // / Terminal Gate brackets: an animated spinner while running, a settled check/X/\"?\" glyph once\n    // finished — driven by an OPTIONAL per-node status map plus an INDEPENDENT includeRefresh\n    // toggle, mirroring LogSiteRenderer.IndexHtml(..., includeRefresh)'s during-run/final duality.\n    //\n    // These tests are structural/string-content assertions over the emitted HTML/JS (no headless\n    // browser is configured in this repo — a documented Level-A gap): they prove the right markup\n    // and data are EMITTED, not that a browser positions the badges pixel-correctly at runtime. The\n    // four non-null-status tests are the intended TDD RED against the throwing stub — the\n    // 02-implement-diagram-status-overlay-renderer task turns them green.\n    //\n    // Status-map ids use the SAME vocabulary MermaidRenderer emits (task containers `task_<base>`,\n    // preflight/guardrail leaves `task_<base>_pf_<n>`/`task_<base>_gr_<n>`, and the two plan-level\n    // brackets `plan_preflights`/`plan_guardrails`) so the post-render overlay script can position a\n    // badge on the matching SVG node. All five status values are exercised.\n    private static readonly IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> SampleStatuses =\n        new Dictionary<string, string>(StringComparer.Ordinal)\n        {\n            [\"plan_preflights\"] = \"passed\",       // Full Flight Checks bracket (top)\n            [\"task_root\"] = \"running\",            // a task container, mid-run -> spinner\n            [\"task_root_pf_0\"] = \"passed\",        // a preflight leaf check\n            [\"task_root_gr_0\"] = \"failed\",        // a guardrail leaf check\n            [\"task_next\"] = \"pending\",            // a not-yet-started task container\n            [\"plan_guardrails\"] = \"needs-human\",  // Terminal Gate bracket (bottom)\n        };\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_WithNullNodeStatuses_IsByteIdenticalToCurrentBehavior()\n    {\n        // The static `graph` command path (no live status) must be UNCHANGED by this feature: the\n        // pre-existing three-argument overload and the new call passing nodeStatuses:null must\n        // produce the exact same document, byte-for-byte — the golden fixtures\n        // (examples/hello-guardrails, docs/plans/08-parallel-execution/diagram.html) are out of this\n        // task's scope and must not need regenerating.\n        string legacy = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget);\n        string newNull = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget, nodeStatuses: null);\n\n        Assert.Equal(legacy, newNull);\n\n        // ...and the static path carries NONE of the live-overlay markers. Each of these is absent\n        // from today's template, so their absence pins the null path clean — a leak of the feature\n        // into the static path (which would silently change every checked-in diagram.html) fails here.\n        Assert.DoesNotContain(\"http-equiv=\\\"refresh\\\"\", newNull, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.DoesNotContain(\"@keyframes\", newNull, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.DoesNotContain(\"id=\\\"node-statuses\\\"\", newNull, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_WithNodeStatuses_EmitsAMetaRefreshTag()\n    {\n        // A non-null status map with the default includeRefresh:true is the DURING-RUN diagram — it\n        // must carry <meta http-equiv=\"refresh\"> so a plain file:// view re-reads itself as the run\n        // progresses (mirrors LogSiteRenderer's during-run index). The static (null) path must not.\n        string live = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget, SampleStatuses);\n        Assert.Contains(\"<meta http-equiv=\\\"refresh\\\"\", live, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n\n        string stat = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget, nodeStatuses: null);\n        Assert.DoesNotContain(\"http-equiv=\\\"refresh\\\"\", stat, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_WithNodeStatusesAndIncludeRefreshFalse_OmitsTheMetaRefreshTag()\n    {\n        // The FINAL settled render (wired at run-end by 06-wire-diagramobserver-into-runcommand):\n        // nodeStatuses is STILL non-null (every node shows its final settled status) but\n        // includeRefresh:false, so the auto-reload tag is dropped — the page is done refreshing. The\n        // status overlay itself must STILL be emitted (the refresh tag and the overlay are independent).\n        string settled = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(\n            Source, Hash, OneTarget, SampleStatuses, includeRefresh: false);\n\n        Assert.DoesNotContain(\"http-equiv=\\\"refresh\\\"\", settled, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        // still a live-status document — the overlay data is present regardless of includeRefresh.\n        Assert.Contains(\"id=\\\"node-statuses\\\"\", settled, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.Contains(\"\\\"task_root\\\"\", settled, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_WithNodeStatuses_EmitsAnOverlayForEachStatusEntry()\n    {\n        // Every node id in the status map must be referenced by the overlay-rendering logic — the\n        // map is embedded as a JSON side-table (mirroring the task-folder-targets side-table) keyed\n        // by the SAME Mermaid node/container ids, so the post-render script can position a badge on\n        // each matching SVG node. Assert the QUOTED (JSON-key) form: a bare-word check would false-\n        // positive on ids like `plan_guardrails` that ALREADY appear in a code comment in today's\n        // template — only the emitted status map produces the quoted form.\n        string live = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget, SampleStatuses);\n\n        foreach (string nodeId in SampleStatuses.Keys)\n        {\n            Assert.Contains($\"\\\"{nodeId}\\\"\", live, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        }\n    }\n\n    [Fact]\n    public void Render_WithRunningStatus_EmitsASpinnerClass_AndSettledStatusesEmitAGlyph()\n    {\n        // \"running\" must render an ANIMATED spinner (a CSS @keyframes rotation — no external\n        // image/GIF dependency), visibly distinct from a settled status's STATIC glyph (check / X /\n        // \"?\"). Assert both the spinner animation + its dedicated class AND at least one settled\n        // glyph are present; the spinner marker (a CSS class) is inherently distinct from the glyph\n        // characters, so a spinner can never be mistaken for a settled state.\n        string live = HtmlDiagramRenderer.Render(Source, Hash, OneTarget, SampleStatuses);\n\n        // spinner: a CSS keyframes rotation + a dedicated class (neither exists in the static template).\n        Assert.Contains(\"@keyframes\", live, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.Contains(\"status-spinner\", live, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n\n        // settled glyphs: `passed` -> U+2713 CHECK MARK, `failed` -> U+2717 BALLOT X (both present in\n        // SampleStatuses). Written as literal UTF-8 glyphs; this file is valid UTF-8, which Roslyn's\n        // BOM-less source detection decodes as UTF-8, so the literals compile to exactly these chars.\n        Assert.Contains(\"✓\", live, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        Assert.Contains(\"✗\", live, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n}\n","numLines":459,"startLine":1,"totalLines":459}}}

This is not a rendering accident —\n377\t    /// with the nested boxes gone, source order is the only surviving signal that preflights run\n378\t    /// BEFORE the task's attempt loop and guardrails run AFTER it, so callers (and the legend) may\n379\t    /// rely on it as a stable convention.\n380\t    /// </remarks>\n381\t    /// <remarks>\n382\t    /// No anchor node of any kind is emitted here (issue #211's mechanism was removed entirely —\n383\t    /// issue #235; see class remarks). <see cref=\"Render\"/> and <see cref=\"RenderInteractive\"/> now\n384\t    /// emit byte-identical container/node shape for every task; the container's click target lives\n385\t    /// entirely in <see cref=\"HtmlDiagramRenderer\"/>'s post-render JavaScript overlay instead.\n386\t    /// </remarks>\n387\t    private static void AppendTaskContainer(StringBuilder sb, TaskNode task, string @base)\n388\t    {\n389\t        string containerId = $\"task_{@base}\";\n390\t\n391\t        AppendLf(sb, $\"  subgraph {containerId}[{Quote(task.Id)}]\");\n392\t\n393\t        // Preflights BEFORE guardrails — see remarks: this order is the emission-order contract\n394\t        // that now carries the \"before the attempt loop\" / \"after the action\" temporal semantic\n395\t        // the removed nested boxes used to convey visually.\n396\t        AppendCheckNodes(sb, \"    \", $\"{containerId}_pf\", task.Preflights, \"preflight\");\n397\t        AppendCheckNodes(sb, \"    \", $\"{containerId}_gr\", task.Guardrails, \"guardrail\");\n398\t\n399\t        AppendLf(sb, \"  end\");\n400\t        AppendLf(sb, $\"  style {containerId} {TaskStyle}\");\n401\t    }\n402\t\n403\t    /// <summary>\n404\t    /// Append <paramref name=\"checks\"/> (sorted ordinal by name, for input-order independence) as\n405\t    /// <c>{nodeIdPrefix}_{ordinal}[label]:::{checkClass}</c> node lines, one per check. Drawn label\n406\t    /// is ALWAYS <see cref=\"GuardrailDefinition.Name\"/> — the check's own short, stable identifier\n407\t    /// (the file-derived name, e.g. <c>01-core-tests-green-excluding-target</c>), never the\n408\t    /// (possibly long) <see cref=\"GuardrailDefinition.Description\"/>. A prior version drew the\n409\t    /// description (truncated for task-level preflights only, issue #211) — the owner asked\n410\t    /// instead for the same short, meaningful identifier every box's click target already opens,\n411\t    /// uniformly for every check kind at both scopes (issue #222). The full description remains\n412\t    /// reachable via the node's <c>click</c> tooltip in <see cref=\"RenderInteractive\"/> (issue\n413\t    /// #33's existing click mechanism, unaffected by this change) — no truncation heuristic is\n414\t    /// needed anywhere now.\n415\t    /// </summary>\n416\t    private static void AppendCheckNodes(\n417\t        StringBuilder sb,\n418\t        string indent,\n419\t        string nodeIdPrefix,\n420\t        IReadOnlyList<GuardrailDefinition> checks,\n421\t        string checkClass)\n422\t    {\n423\t        int ordinal = 0;\n424\t        foreach (GuardrailDefinition check in checks.OrderBy(c => c.Name, StringComparer.Ordinal))\n425\t        {\n426\t            AppendLf(sb, $\"{indent}{nodeIdPrefix}_{ordinal}[{Quote(check.Name)}]:::{checkClass}\");\n427\t            ordinal++;\n428\t        }\n429\t    }\n430\t\n431\t    /// <summary>\n432\t    /// Append every container→container edge: the plan-preflights container into each DAG ROOT\n433\t    /// task's container (a task with no <c>dependsOn</c>), one edge per <c>dependsOn</c>\n434\t    /// relationship between two task containers, and each DAG LEAF task's container (a task nothing\n435\t    /// depends on) into the plan-guardrails container. The edge references the container's own\n436\t    /// subgraph id, so Mermaid clips the arrow to the container's OUTER BORDER (issue #210). A\n437\t    /// task-level preflight does not change this — the gated dependency edge is drawn exactly like\n438\t    /// any other; the preflight is only ever a check node inside the consumer's own container\n439\t    /// (emitted before the container's guardrail check nodes — see <see cref=\"AppendTaskContainer\"/>).\n440\t    /// </summary>\n441\t    private static void AppendContainerEdges(\n442\t        DependencyGraph graph,\n443\t        IReadOnlyList<TaskNode> tasks,\n444\t        IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> nodeIdBase,\n445\t        StringBuilder sb)\n446\t    {\n447\t        foreach (TaskNode root in tasks.Where(t => t.DependsOn.Count == 0))\n448\t        {\n449\t            AppendLf(sb, $\"  {PlanPreflightsId} --> task_{nodeIdBase[root.Id]}\");\n450\t        }\n451\t\n452\t        foreach (TaskNode dependency in tasks)\n453\t        {\n454\t            foreach (string dependentId in graph.DependentsOf(dependency.Id)\n455\t                         .OrderBy(id => id, StringComparer.Ordinal))\n456\t            {\n457\t                AppendLf(sb, $\"  task_{nodeIdBase[dependency.Id]} --> task_{nodeIdBase[dependentId]}\");\n458\t            }\n459\t        }\n460\t\n461\t        foreach (TaskNode leaf in tasks.Where(t => graph.DependentsOf(t.Id).Count == 0))\n462\t        {\n463\t            AppendLf(sb, $\"  task_{nodeIdBase[leaf.Id]} --> {PlanGuardrailsId}\");\n464\t        }\n465\t    }\n466\t\n467\t    /// <summary>\n468\t    /// Append <c>click</c> directives (HTML-viewer only; see <see cref=\"RenderInteractive\"/>) for\n469\t    /// every CHECK node — plan-level or task-level, preflight or guardrail — opening its own file\n470\t    /// as a plan-relative, forward-slash <c>file://</c> target resolved relative to\n471\t    /// <c>diagram.html</c> at the plan root, opened in a new tab (<c>_blank</c>) so the diagram\n472\t    /// stays put. Emitted in the same ordinal/sorted order as the nodes for determinism, and using\n473\t    /// the SAME node-id scheme as <see cref=\"AppendNodesAndEdges\"/> so every click target actually\n474\t    /// exists. A task-level preflight's click tooltip carries its FULL description (not just its\n475\t    /// name) since <see cref=\"AppendCheckNodes\"/> draws only a truncated label for it — the\n476\t    /// tooltip is the click-for-detail mechanism that keeps the full text from being lost.\n477\t    /// </summary>\n478\t    /// <remarks>\n479\t    /// <b>No container click directive is emitted here (issue #235).</b> A task container's click\n480\t    /// target is no longer a Mermaid mechanism at all — see class remarks, \"A task container's click\n481\t    /// target is a POST-RENDER SVG overlay...\". <see cref=\"HtmlDiagramRenderer\"/> injects it via\n482\t    /// JavaScript after Mermaid's render completes, using <see cref=\"TaskFolderTargets\"/> for the\n483\t    /// folder path data. Leaf check-node clicks are unaffected here: they still target the leaf node\n484\t    /// itself, which Mermaid DOES wrap in a real clickable <c>&lt;a href&gt;</c>.\n485\t    /// </remarks>\n486\t    private static void AppendClickDirectives(\n487\t        PlanDefinition plan, IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> nodeIdBase, StringBuilder sb)\n488\t    {\n489\t        AppendCheckClicks(plan, plan.PlanPreflights, PlanPreflightsId, sb);\n490\t\n491\t        foreach (TaskNode task in plan.Tasks.OrderBy(t => t.Id, StringComparer.Ordinal))\n492\t        {\n493\t            string @base = nodeIdBase[task.Id];\n494\t            string containerId = $\"task_{@base}\";\n495\t\n496\t            if (task.Preflights.Count > 0)\n497\t            {\n498\t                AppendCheckClicks(plan, task.Preflights, $\"{containerId}_pf\", sb);\n499\t            }\n500\t\n501\t            AppendCheckClicks(plan, task.Guardrails, $\"{containerId}_gr\", sb);\n502\t        }\n503\t\n504\t        AppendCheckClicks(plan, plan.PlanGuardrails, PlanGuardrailsId, sb);\n505\t    }\n506\t\n507\t    /// <summary>\n508\t    /// Append one <c>click</c> directive per check in <paramref name=\"checks\"/> (sorted ordinal by\n509\t    /// name, mirroring <see cref=\"AppendCheckNodes\"/> exactly so the ordinal-suffixed node id each"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"947025b1-00ab-45d6-bec4-5dec3305bac9","uuid":"2ae453c8-00a8-48f5-8bf9-b9a3f834643e","timestamp":"2026-07-07T16:18:38.103Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"C:\\Users\\David\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\guardrails-worktrees\\diagram-live-status-and-search-80c8913d\\1bb6c1ff\\07-author-tests-diagram-search-box\\attempt-1\\src\\Guardrails.Core\\Graph\\MermaidRenderer.cs","content":"    /// <c>Preflights</c>/<c>Guardrails</c> wrapper subgraph (see class remarks, \"Nested boxes\n    /// dropped\") — then the container's <c>style</c> fill. The DAG edge attaches to this\n    /// container's own subgraph id (no interior anchor).\n    /// </summary>\n    /// <remarks>\n    /// <b>Emission-order contract (load-bearing, tested):</b> preflight check nodes are ALWAYS\n    /// emitted before guardrail check nodes within a container. This is not a rendering accident —\n    /// with the nested boxes gone, source order is the only surviving signal that preflights run\n    /// BEFORE the task's attempt loop and guardrails run AFTER it, so callers (and the legend) may\n    /// rely on it as a stable convention.\n    /// </remarks>\n    /// <remarks>\n    /// No anchor node of any kind is emitted here (issue #211's mechanism was removed entirely —\n    /// issue #235; see class remarks). <see cref=\"Render\"/> and <see cref=\"RenderInteractive\"/> now\n    /// emit byte-identical container/node shape for every task; the container's click target lives\n    /// entirely in <see cref=\"HtmlDiagramRenderer\"/>'s post-render JavaScript overlay instead.\n    /// </remarks>\n    private static void AppendTaskContainer(StringBuilder sb, TaskNode task, string @base)\n    {\n        string containerId = $\"task_{@base}\";\n\n        AppendLf(sb, $\"  subgraph {containerId}[{Quote(task.Id)}]\");\n\n        // Preflights BEFORE guardrails — see remarks: this order is the emission-order contract\n        // that now carries the \"before the attempt loop\" / \"after the action\" temporal semantic\n        // the removed nested boxes used to convey visually.\n        AppendCheckNodes(sb, \"    \", $\"{containerId}_pf\", task.Preflights, \"preflight\");\n        AppendCheckNodes(sb, \"    \", $\"{containerId}_gr\", task.Guardrails, \"guardrail\");\n\n        AppendLf(sb, \"  end\");\n        AppendLf(sb, $\"  style {containerId} {TaskStyle}\");\n    }\n\n    /// <summary>\n    /// Append <paramref name=\"checks\"/> (sorted ordinal by name, for input-order independence) as\n    /// <c>{nodeIdPrefix}_{ordinal}[label]:::{checkClass}</c> node lines, one per check. Drawn label\n    /// is ALWAYS <see cref=\"GuardrailDefinition.Name\"/> — the check's own short, stable identifier\n    /// (the file-derived name, e.g. <c>01-core-tests-green-excluding-target</c>), never the\n    /// (possibly long) <see cref=\"GuardrailDefinition.Description\"/>. A prior version drew the\n    /// description (truncated for task-level preflights only, issue #211) — the owner asked\n    /// instead for the same short, meaningful identifier every box's click target already opens,\n    /// uniformly for every check kind at both scopes (issue #222). The full description remains\n    /// reachable via the node's <c>click</c> tooltip in <see cref=\"RenderInteractive\"/> (issue\n    /// #33's existing click mechanism, unaffected by this change) — no truncation heuristic is\n    /// needed anywhere now.\n    /// </summary>\n    private static void AppendCheckNodes(\n        StringBuilder sb,\n        string indent,\n        string nodeIdPrefix,\n        IReadOnlyList<GuardrailDefinition> checks,\n        string checkClass)\n    {\n        int ordinal = 0;\n        foreach (GuardrailDefinition check in checks.OrderBy(c => c.Name, StringComparer.Ordinal))\n        {\n            AppendLf(sb, $\"{indent}{nodeIdPrefix}_{ordinal}[{Quote(check.Name)}]:::{checkClass}\");\n            ordinal++;\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// <summary>\n    /// Append every container→container edge: the plan-preflights container into each DAG ROOT\n    /// task's container (a task with no <c>dependsOn</c>), one edge per <c>dependsOn</c>\n    /// relationship between two task containers, and each DAG LEAF task's container (a task nothing\n    /// depends on) into the plan-guardrails container. The edge references the container's own\n    /// subgraph id, so Mermaid clips the arrow to the container's OUTER BORDER (issue #210). A\n    /// task-level preflight does not change this — the gated dependency edge is drawn exactly like\n    /// any other; the preflight is only ever a check node inside the consumer's own container\n    /// (emitted before the container's guardrail check nodes — see <see cref=\"AppendTaskContainer\"/>).\n    /// </summary>\n    private static void AppendContainerEdges(\n        DependencyGraph graph,\n        IReadOnlyList<TaskNode> tasks,\n        IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> nodeIdBase,\n        StringBuilder sb)\n    {\n        foreach (TaskNode root in tasks.Where(t => t.DependsOn.Count == 0))\n        {\n            AppendLf(sb, $\"  {PlanPreflightsId} --> task_{nodeIdBase[root.Id]}\");\n        }\n\n        foreach (TaskNode dependency in tasks)\n        {\n            foreach (string dependentId in graph.DependentsOf(dependency.Id)\n                         .OrderBy(id => id, StringComparer.Ordinal))\n            {\n                AppendLf(sb, $\"  task_{nodeIdBase[dependency.Id]} --> task_{nodeIdBase[dependentId]}\");\n            }\n        }\n\n        foreach (TaskNode leaf in tasks.Where(t => graph.DependentsOf(t.Id).Count == 0))\n        {\n            AppendLf(sb, $\"  task_{nodeIdBase[leaf.Id]} --> {PlanGuardrailsId}\");\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// <summary>\n    /// Append <c>click</c> directives (HTML-viewer only; see <see cref=\"RenderInteractive\"/>) for\n    /// every CHECK node — plan-level or task-level, preflight or guardrail — opening its own file\n    /// as a plan-relative, forward-slash <c>file://</c> target resolved relative to\n    /// <c>diagram.html</c> at the plan root, opened in a new tab (<c>_blank</c>) so the diagram\n    /// stays put. Emitted in the same ordinal/sorted order as the nodes for determinism, and using\n    /// the SAME node-id scheme as <see cref=\"AppendNodesAndEdges\"/> so every click target actually\n    /// exists. A task-level preflight's click tooltip carries its FULL description (not just its\n    /// name) since <see cref=\"AppendCheckNodes\"/> draws only a truncated label for it — the\n    /// tooltip is the click-for-detail mechanism that keeps the full text from being lost.\n    /// </summary>\n    /// <remarks>\n    /// <b>No container click directive is emitted here (issue #235).</b> A task container's click\n    /// target is no longer a Mermaid mechanism at all — see class remarks, \"A task container's click\n    /// target is a POST-RENDER SVG overlay...\". <see cref=\"HtmlDiagramRenderer\"/> injects it via\n    /// JavaScript after Mermaid's render completes, using <see cref=\"TaskFolderTargets\"/> for the\n    /// folder path data. Leaf check-node clicks are unaffected here: they still target the leaf node\n    /// itself, which Mermaid DOES wrap in a real clickable <c>&lt;a href&gt;</c>.\n    /// </remarks>\n    private static void AppendClickDirectives(\n        PlanDefinition plan, IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> nodeIdBase, StringBuilder sb)\n    {\n        AppendCheckClicks(plan, plan.PlanPreflights, PlanPreflightsId, sb);\n\n        foreach (TaskNode task in plan.Tasks.OrderBy(t => t.Id, StringComparer.Ordinal))\n        {\n            string @base = nodeIdBase[task.Id];\n            string containerId = $\"task_{@base}\";\n\n            if (task.Preflights.Count > 0)\n            {\n                AppendCheckClicks(plan, task.Preflights, $\"{containerId}_pf\", sb);\n            }\n\n            AppendCheckClicks(plan, task.Guardrails, $\"{containerId}_gr\", sb);\n        }\n\n        AppendCheckClicks(plan, plan.PlanGuardrails, PlanGuardrailsId, sb);\n    }\n\n    /// <summary>\n    /// Append one <c>click</c> directive per check in <paramref name=\"checks\"/> (sorted ordinal by\n    /// name, mirroring <see cref=\"AppendCheckNodes\"/> exactly so the ordinal-suffixed node id each","numLines":140,"startLine":370,"totalLines":648}}}

(file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"947025b1-00ab-45d6-bec4-5dec3305bac9","uuid":"dc2f5837-a4d6-4555-8d34-31cc38ebdc6d","timestamp":"2026-07-07T16:27:49.195Z","tool_use_result":{"filePath":"C:\\Users\\David\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\guardrails-worktrees\\diagram-live-status-and-search-80c8913d\\1bb6c1ff\\07-author-tests-diagram-search-box\\attempt-1\\src\\Guardrails.Core\\Graph\\HtmlDiagramRenderer.cs","oldString":"/// (including the whole golden <c>hello-guardrails</c> example) was left byte-for-byte unchanged.\n/// </para>\n/// </remarks>\npublic static class HtmlDiagramRenderer","newString":"/// (including the whole golden <c>hello-guardrails</c> example) was left byte-for-byte unchanged.\n/// </para>\n/// <para>\n/// <b>Search box (issue #220).</b> A fixed-position <c>#search-box</c> <c>&lt;div&gt;</c> (same\n/// overlay technique as <c>#legend</c>/<c>#bar</c>/<c>#hint</c> and the status badges) is emitted\n/// UNCONDITIONALLY — unlike the live status overlay above, search does not depend on the\n/// <c>nodeStatuses</c> parameter (see <see cref=\"Render\"/>) being non-null, so it is present on both\n/// the static <c>graph</c> output and the live/final run diagrams. The search-matching data (every\n/// node id + visible label) is embedded the same way as\n/// <see cref=\"MermaidRenderer.TaskFolderTargets\"/> — a <c>&lt;script type=\"application/json\"\n/// id=\"search-index\"&gt;</c> side-table read back via <c>textContent</c> — built by\n/// <see cref=\"BuildSearchIndexJson\"/>. <b>This is a stub</b>: it always emits an empty object, and\n/// the embedded <c>runSearch</c> script throws (a deliberate TDD red for\n/// <c>08-implement-diagram-search-box</c>) — see that method's remarks.\n/// </para>\n/// </remarks>\npublic static class HtmlDiagramRenderer","originalFile":"using System.Text.Encodings.Web;\nusing System.Text.Json;\n\nnamespace Guardrails.Core.Graph;\n\n/// <summary>\n/// Renders the local-viewing companion to <c>diagram.md</c>: a self-contained\n/// <c>diagram.html</c> that displays the SAME Mermaid DAG with pan / zoom / fullscreen, so a\n/// large task+guardrail graph is actually navigable on disk (GitHub renders <c>diagram.md</c>\n/// but offers no navigation). Pure: maps the rendered Mermaid text + its <c>source-sha256</c>\n/// to an HTML string with no I/O (issue #33).\n/// </summary>\n/// <remarks>\n/// <para>\n/// The Mermaid source is embedded VERBATIM as the text content of a\n/// <c>&lt;script type=\"text/plain\"&gt;</c> element and read back via <c>textContent</c> — never\n/// interpolated into a JS string. This sidesteps every escaping hazard (a label containing a\n/// backtick, <c>${</c>, or a quote cannot break the page), and a <c>&lt;script&gt;</c> element's\n/// content is \"raw text\" so entities are not decoded — the source round-trips byte-for-byte.\n/// This is safe because <see cref=\"MermaidRenderer\"/> HTML-escapes every label (so <c>&lt;</c>\n/// becomes <c>&amp;lt;</c>), meaning the source can never contain <c>&lt;/script&gt;</c>.\n/// </para>\n/// <para>\n/// The <c>source-sha256</c> provenance comment is emitted as the FIRST line (before\n/// <c>&lt;!doctype html&gt;</c>) so the same <c>\\A</c>-anchored reader that validates\n/// <c>diagram.md</c> validates this file too (<c>graph --check</c>). A comment before the\n/// doctype does not trigger quirks mode.\n/// </para>\n/// <para>\n/// The renderer (Mermaid) and pan-zoom library load from a CDN, so the interactive view needs\n/// internet the first time. GitHub will not execute the embedded script — this file is the\n/// LOCAL artifact; <c>diagram.md</c> remains the portal artifact. Fully offline (inlined assets)\n/// is a possible follow-up.\n/// </para>\n/// <para>\n/// <b>Legend overlay.</b> A corner-anchored <c>#legend</c> <c>&lt;div&gt;</c>\n/// (<c>position: fixed</c>), mirroring the existing <c>#bar</c>/<c>#hint</c> overlay divs, renders\n/// <see cref=\"MermaidRenderer.LegendMarkdown\"/>'s content OUTSIDE the Mermaid SVG. A Mermaid-native\n/// legend (a disconnected subgraph of colour-swatch nodes) was prototyped and rendered BROKEN —\n/// dagre lays out a disconnected subgraph as a phantom extra \"task\" overlapping the real DAG — so\n/// the overlay div is the only approach that renders correctly. Static HTML, not templated from\n/// the Mermaid source, so it carries no bearing on <c>source-sha256</c>.\n/// </para>\n/// <para>\n/// <b>Task-container click target: a POST-RENDER SVG title-band overlay (issue #232/#233\n/// superseded, issue #235).</b> A Mermaid <c>click</c> directive never fires on a subgraph/cluster\n/// element (upstream limitation; see <see cref=\"MermaidRenderer\"/> remarks), and the first fix\n/// attempt — an invisible anchor NODE inside the container — proved useless in practice: dagre\n/// sizes and packs it into whatever gap its own layout leaves, which for a content-dense container\n/// is a tiny, off-center sliver (measured: 0.44% of the container's area on a real 4-guardrail\n/// task). The fix implemented here instead runs AFTER <c>mermaid.render</c> resolves: for every\n/// <c>g.cluster</c> element whose id starts with <c>task_</c>, compute a full-width band from the\n/// cluster's own bounding box down to just past its <c>.cluster-label</c>'s bottom edge (Mermaid\n/// always reserves this header strip above any leaf content, so it is empty BY CONSTRUCTION\n/// regardless of how many guardrails/preflights the task has — unlike an interior anchor node) and\n/// append a real <c>&lt;a href=\"...\" target=\"_blank\"&gt;&lt;rect fill=\"transparent\"&gt;&lt;/a&gt;</c>\n/// spanning it. APPENDED, not inserted first: a cluster's only two original children are its\n/// background <c>&lt;rect&gt;</c> then its <c>.cluster-label</c> group, so appending puts the\n/// overlay last in paint order (on top, clickable) without moving in front of the label text\n/// visually (the rect is transparent) and — because every leaf check node lives in an entirely\n/// separate top-level SVG group from its own container's <c>g.cluster</c> — the overlay can never\n/// occlude or be occluded by a leaf node's own click target either way. The task→folder-path data\n/// this script needs (<see cref=\"MermaidRenderer.TaskFolderTargets\"/>) is embedded as a small JSON\n/// object keyed by the SAME container id the Mermaid source uses, in a\n/// <c>&lt;script type=\"application/json\"&gt;</c> element read back via <c>textContent</c> (same\n/// verbatim/never-interpolated treatment as the Mermaid source itself, immune to the same escaping\n/// hazards).\n/// </para>\n/// <para>\n/// <b>Long task-name title wrap-overflow, fixed by widening the label's foreignObject\n/// post-render (issue cluster-label-wrap-overflow).</b> Mermaid always wraps a cluster's title\n/// <c>&lt;div&gt;</c> to a hardcoded 200px width (the bundled <c>mermaid@11.4.1</c>'s plain\n/// flowchart cluster shape never overrides <c>createText</c>'s <c>width = 200</c> default,\n/// regardless of the container's own — usually much wider — computed width), and dagre's layout\n/// pass reserves the container's header-strip height BEFORE that wrapped height is known, so a\n/// long kebab-case task name (hyphens are valid soft line-break points) that wraps to 2+ lines\n/// prints past the reserved strip, overlapping the first leaf guardrail/preflight box positioned\n/// directly below. No Mermaid config knob avoids this — <c>flowchart.htmlLabels</c> only toggles\n/// the html-vs-svg-text label renderer, and 11.4.1 has no documented option for cluster-label\n/// wrap width. The fix (the <c>fixWrappedClusterLabels</c> function, run AFTER\n/// <c>mermaid.render</c> resolves and BEFORE the title-band overlay above, since the overlay's\n/// band height depends on the label's — by then possibly shrunk — bounding box) re-wraps the\n/// SAME text at up to the container's own width instead: since the container is normally already\n/// wider than 200px, this almost always drops the label to one line, which needs LESS height than\n/// the original wrap — never more — so no other node/edge/container ever needs to move. Verified\n/// headless against 8+ real plans (40+ long task names): every wrapped case converged to one line\n/// with the same healthy gap a never-wrapped label already has, and every already-fits label\n/// (including the whole golden <c>hello-guardrails</c> example) was left byte-for-byte unchanged.\n/// </para>\n/// </remarks>\npublic static class HtmlDiagramRenderer\n{\n    /// <summary>\n    /// Build the <c>diagram.html</c> document for <paramref name=\"mermaidSource\"/> (the exact\n    /// text rendered into <c>diagram.md</c>, including the <c>flowchart TD</c> header and the\n    /// cosmetic <c>classDef</c> lines) stamped with <paramref name=\"sourceHash\"/>. <paramref\n    /// name=\"taskFolderTargets\"/> is the task-container-id → plan-relative-folder-path map (see\n    /// <see cref=\"MermaidRenderer.TaskFolderTargets\"/>) the embedded title-band overlay script uses\n    /// to resolve each container's click target (issue #235 — see class remarks).\n    /// </summary>\n    /// <param name=\"nodeStatuses\">\n    /// OPTIONAL live-run status map (issue #219): Mermaid node/container id → one of\n    /// <c>\"pending\"</c>, <c>\"running\"</c>, <c>\"passed\"</c>, <c>\"failed\"</c>, <c>\"needs-human\"</c>,\n    /// keyed by the SAME ids <see cref=\"MermaidRenderer\"/> emits (task containers <c>task_&lt;base&gt;</c>,\n    /// preflight/guardrail leaves <c>task_&lt;base&gt;_pf_&lt;n&gt;</c>/<c>task_&lt;base&gt;_gr_&lt;n&gt;</c>,\n    /// and the plan-level brackets <c>plan_preflights</c>/<c>plan_guardrails</c>). When non-null the\n    /// document additionally carries a per-node status-overlay badge (an animated spinner while\n    /// <c>running</c>, a settled check/X/\"?\" glyph once finished). When <c>null</c> (the static\n    /// <c>graph</c> command, which never runs live) the output is byte-identical to the pre-#219\n    /// three-argument render.\n    /// </param>\n    /// <param name=\"includeRefresh\">\n    /// INDEPENDENT of the status overlay (mirrors <c>LogSiteRenderer.IndexHtml(..., includeRefresh)</c>):\n    /// when <paramref name=\"nodeStatuses\"/> is non-null AND this is <c>true</c> (the default,\n    /// the DURING-RUN diagram) a <c>&lt;meta http-equiv=\"refresh\" content=\"2\"&gt;</c> is emitted so a\n    /// plain <c>file://</c> view re-reads itself as the run progresses; when <c>false</c> (the FINAL\n    /// settled render wired at run-end by <c>06-wire-diagramobserver-into-runcommand</c>) the overlay\n    /// is still emitted but the refresh tag is not. Ignored when <paramref name=\"nodeStatuses\"/> is null.\n    /// </param>\n    public static string Render(\n        string mermaidSource, string sourceHash, IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> taskFolderTargets,\n        IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string>? nodeStatuses = null, bool includeRefresh = true)\n    {\n        ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(mermaidSource);\n        ArgumentException.ThrowIfNullOrEmpty(sourceHash);\n        ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(taskFolderTargets);\n\n        // Newline-normalize so the file is byte-identical across OSes (mirrors the renderer/hash).\n        string source = mermaidSource\n            .Replace(\"\\r\\n\", \"\\n\", StringComparison.Ordinal)\n            .Replace(\"\\r\", \"\\n\", StringComparison.Ordinal)\n            .TrimEnd('\\n');\n\n        // Encoder that escapes NOTHING beyond what JSON strictly requires (default System.Text.Json\n        // escapes '<', '>', '&', etc. as \\uXXXX for HTML safety, which is unnecessary here — the\n        // JSON sits inside a <script type=\"application/json\"> element, read back via textContent,\n        // exactly like the Mermaid source above — but using the unsafe-relaxed encoder keeps a\n        // task-id containing e.g. \"&\" readable in the raw HTML source without changing behavior).\n        string targetsJson = JsonSerializer.Serialize(taskFolderTargets, new JsonSerializerOptions\n        {\n            Encoder = JavaScriptEncoder.UnsafeRelaxedJsonEscaping,\n        });\n\n        string html = Template\n            .Replace(\"__SOURCE_SHA256__\", sourceHash, StringComparison.Ordinal)\n            .Replace(\"__GRAPH_SOURCE__\", source, StringComparison.Ordinal)\n            .Replace(\"__TASK_FOLDER_TARGETS__\", targetsJson, StringComparison.Ordinal);\n\n        // Live-run status overlay (issue #219) is OPTIONAL: when nodeStatuses is null (the static\n        // `graph` command, which never runs live) the template is emitted UNCHANGED, so the output\n        // stays byte-identical to the pre-#219 three-argument render. When provided, inject the\n        // per-node status badges + CSS, the node-statuses side-table, and — when includeRefresh — the\n        // auto-reload meta tag (see InjectStatusOverlay).\n        if (nodeStatuses is not null)\n        {\n            html = InjectStatusOverlay(html, nodeStatuses, includeRefresh);\n        }\n\n        // Normalize the full output — the template raw-string literal (and the injected blocks above)\n        // pick up \\r\\n when the file is checked out with CRLF on Windows; the mermaid source is\n        // already normalized above.\n        return html\n            .Replace(\"\\r\\n\", \"\\n\", StringComparison.Ordinal)\n            .Replace(\"\\r\", \"\\n\", StringComparison.Ordinal);\n    }\n\n    /// <summary>\n    /// Inject the live-run status overlay (issue #219) into the base <paramref name=\"html\"/>: the\n    /// per-node status-badge markup + CSS, the <c>#node-statuses</c> JSON side-table, and — when\n    /// <paramref name=\"includeRefresh\"/> — the <c>&lt;meta http-equiv=\"refresh\"&gt;</c> auto-reload\n    /// tag. Called ONLY on the non-null path (see <see cref=\"Render\"/>), so the static-graph output is\n    /// left byte-identical.\n    /// </summary>\n    /// <remarks>\n    /// Mirrors the existing title-band overlay's post-render-script technique: the badges are HTML\n    /// overlay <c>&lt;div&gt;</c>s (like <c>#bar</c>/<c>#legend</c>) rendered OUTSIDE the SVG and\n    /// anchored to each node's on-screen box via <c>getBoundingClientRect()</c>. Because they live in\n    /// screen space rather than inside the SVG, they are re-anchored on every <c>svg-pan-zoom</c>\n    /// pan/zoom (wired through the pan-zoom instance's <c>onPan</c>/<c>onZoom</c> callbacks) and on\n    /// window resize. A <c>running</c> node shows an animated CSS-<c>@keyframes</c> spinner (no\n    /// external image); every other (settled) status shows a static glyph. The auto-reload tag is\n    /// INDEPENDENT of the overlay (mirrors <c>LogSiteRenderer.IndexHtml(..., includeRefresh)</c>'s\n    /// during-run vs final duality) — present for the during-run diagram, dropped for the final\n    /// settled render.\n    /// </remarks>\n    private static string InjectStatusOverlay(\n        string html, IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> nodeStatuses, bool includeRefresh)\n    {\n        // Same relaxed-encoder side-table treatment as taskFolderTargets: a JSON object (node id ->\n        // status word) read back via textContent from a <script type=\"application/json\"> element.\n        string statusesJson = JsonSerializer.Serialize(nodeStatuses, new JsonSerializerOptions\n        {\n            Encoder = JavaScriptEncoder.UnsafeRelaxedJsonEscaping,\n        });\n\n        // Auto-reload tag (during-run only) right after the viewport meta in <head>.\n        if (includeRefresh)\n        {\n            html = html.Replace(\n                \"<meta name=\\\"viewport\\\" content=\\\"width=device-width, initial-scale=1\\\">\",\n                \"<meta name=\\\"viewport\\\" content=\\\"width=device-width, initial-scale=1\\\">\\n\"\n                    + \"<meta http-equiv=\\\"refresh\\\" content=\\\"2\\\">\",\n                StringComparison.Ordinal);\n        }\n\n        // Status-badge CSS (spinner @keyframes + per-status colours) just before </style>.\n        html = html.Replace(\n            \"</style>\", StatusOverlayStyle + \"\\n</style>\", StringComparison.Ordinal);\n\n        // The node id -> status side-table, mirroring the task-folder-targets side-table, placed just\n        // before the svg-pan-zoom script so it is already in the DOM when the module script reads it.\n        html = html.Replace(\n            \"<script src=\\\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/svg-pan-zoom\",\n            \"<script type=\\\"application/json\\\" id=\\\"node-statuses\\\">\" + statusesJson + \"</script>\\n\"\n                + \"<script src=\\\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/svg-pan-zoom\",\n            StringComparison.Ordinal);\n\n        // The overlay functions, defined just before `let pz = null;` (module scope, after the graph/\n        // targets consts, so they can read #node-statuses and be called from the try block below).\n        html = html.Replace(\n            \"let pz = null;\", StatusOverlayScript + \"\\n\\nlet pz = null;\", StringComparison.Ordinal);\n\n        // Build the overlay on the SAME SVG mermaid.render just produced, right after the title-band\n        // overlay (so it measures the SVG in its final, wrap-corrected shape).\n        html = html.Replace(\n            \"  addTaskContainerOverlays(el);\",\n            \"  addTaskContainerOverlays(el);\\n  addStatusOverlays(el);\",\n            StringComparison.Ordinal);\n\n        // Re-anchor the (screen-space) badges whenever the pan-zoom viewport pans or zooms.\n        html = html.Replace(\n            \"minZoom: 0.1, maxZoom: 20, zoomScaleSensitivity: 0.3 });\",\n            \"minZoom: 0.1, maxZoom: 20, zoomScaleSensitivity: 0.3,\\n\"\n                + \"                        onPan: positionStatusBadges, onZoom: positionStatusBadges });\",\n            StringComparison.Ordinal);\n\n        // ...and on resize, plus one initial placement now that pan-zoom has fit the diagram.\n        html = html.Replace(\n            \"  window.addEventListener('resize', () => { pz.resize(); pz.fit(); pz.center(); });\",\n            \"  window.addEventListener('resize', () => { pz.resize(); pz.fit(); pz.center(); positionStatusBadges(); });\\n\"\n                + \"  positionStatusBadges();\",\n
